run.researchNotes: Top-up 2, 16 Nov 2026, 2 further searches. global.cagr y15, y10 and y3: McKinsey's archive (2014-2022 reviews) and the 2026 review were searched for a banking-revenue series on the 2025 basis ($6.4tn revenues before risk costs). None was found that gives a 2010, 2015 or 2022 figure on that basis. The only 2023 figure found ($6.8tn) is total revenue from global financial intermediation, which is a wider measure than bank revenue, so a 3-year CAGR would mix bases. All three keys are omitted. competition.players restated on one measure and one period: reported advances divided by RBI scheduled commercial bank credit of Rs 2,13,61,435 cr, 31 Mar 2026. The residual row is restated on that basis. The 'Public sector banks (12)' row is restated from the Finance Ministry aggregate of PSB gross advances, Rs 127 lakh cr at 31 Mar 2026 (59.45%). That aggregate includes overseas books, so it overstates the domestic share; the Dec 2025 domestic loan share was 54.4%. It is a group total that overlaps the individual PSB rows, so it must not be added to them. 'Private sector banks' and 'Foreign, small finance and other scheduled banks' could not be restated: no aggregate advances figure for 31 Mar 2026 was found for either group. They are Dec 2025 group rows on a different measure that overlap the named banks, and should be deleted from competition.players. A by-name merge cannot remove them.

players.name: Public sector banks (12)
players.basis: bank's reported advances as % of SCB bank credit
players.source: CALCULATION: PSB aggregate gross advances Rs 127 lakh cr at 31 Mar 2026 (Ministry of Finance release, 12 May 2026) / RBI bank credit Rs 2,13,61,435 cr. GROUP TOTAL: overlaps the individual PSB rows; do not sum.

players.name: All other scheduled commercial banks
players.basis: bank's reported advances as % of SCB bank credit
players.source: CALCULATION: 100 minus the eleven named banks (SBI, HDFC, ICICI, BoB, PNB, Axis, Canara, Union, BoI, Indian Bank, Kotak), each on reported advances at 31 Mar 2026 / RBI bank credit Rs 2,13,61,435 cr
